newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Arafat, Ross talk, ministers warn of peace threat.
newsitem.headline: Arafat, Ross talk, ministers warn of peace threat.

text.p: Islamic ministers meeting in Rabat called on Thursday for more support for the Palestinians against Israel's settlement policy in Jerusalem and for a fund to be set up urgently to provide financial help.
Morocco's King Hassan, chairman of the Al-Qods (Jerusalem) Committee, told the closing session: "We should waste no time.

"As soon as possible, we have to set up Beit al-Mal fund, which is in fact a private institution with transparent management, which will enable Moslems around the world to financially participate to support of their Palestinian brothers."
He gave no details of the fund's initial capital.
The Moroccan king said the meeting, which completed its work in "a record time of less than one day for the first time... shows the real maturity of its committee members."
Since its creation in 1976, the committee has held 16 sessions, 15 of them in Morocco under the chairmanship of King Hassan.

The committee meeting coincided with a visit to Rabat by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, who had talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and King Hassan. Ross flew on Thursday to Israel to try to salvage the Middle East peace process, U.S. officials said.
Ross called his talks with Arafat in Rabat "very thorough". He was to hold two meetings in Israel with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Israel last week started building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and there have since been daily clashes on the West Bank between Palestinians and Israelis.

In a statement issued by the U.S. embassy, Ross said: "The purpose of my mission is to make an assessment of the situation in the Middle East for the President (Bill Clinton) and the secretary of state and to report back to them by this weekend."
Neither Ross nor Arafat made any comment to reporters after nearly two hours of talks, underlining the delicate task facing Clinton's envoy in salvaging the peace process.
Arafat and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa made clear before Ross arrived at Arafat's villa that he would be left in no doubt over Arab anger with the policies of Netanyahu.
Moussa told reporters he had talked with the Saudi, Syrian, Gulf and North African foreign ministers -- in Rabat to attend the Al-Qods committee meeting -- and had briefed Arafat on their views.

"Everybody, all of us, are really disturbed over what is going on in Jerusalem. This is the issue. This is the reason why all the repercussions which took place in the occupied territories and in the Middle East have occurred," he said.
Moussa emphasised the Arab view that Israeli policies were to blame for the crisis.
"The problem lies, begins, stems from the policy of settlements in Jerusalem and in the occupied territories. We cannot accept a deviation from that point.
Late on Thursday, the ministers from the 16-member Al-Qods committee met in King Hassan's palace in the Moroccan capital.
The king, who had earlier met Arafat for private talks, said the ministers would examine a draft declaration issued by an Islamic summit in Islamabad earlier this month.

In a live televised ceremony, Arafat told ministers that Jerusalem faced "a dangerous operation of judaisation". He accused Israel of trying to change the demography of Jerusalem "in an attempt to change by force U.N. decisions and resolutions".
Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC) secretary-general Azeddine Laraki told the committee the draft referred to the "dangerous situation" facing Jerusalem from Israel's policy.
It was unclear whether the draft was to be the basis of a resolution from the Al-Qods meeting.

"The Israeli expansionist policy in Jerusalem and other Arab occupied territories...represents a dangerous threat to the peace process," Laraki quoted the draft as saying, adding it urgently called on Israel to stop its policy of settlements.
Laraki said the draft declared support for the Middle East peace process and previous agreements and commitments between Palestinians and Israel, based on land for peace.
It urged Israel to respect its commitments made in Madrid under which the Palestinian people should recover their lands, including Jerusalem.
Israel sees Jerusalem as its eternal capital. The Palestinians say Arab East Jerusalem is the capital of their future state.

Members of the Al-Qods committee are Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Guinea, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Niger, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Pakistan, Senegal, Iraq, Syria, Mauritania and the Palestinian Authority.
